obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses the privileged action manage_payees (rbac.py PRIVILEGED) but is registered with mfa=False. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on the head commit and names this route.
The cited exception EXC-0210 (MFA-1, payments.routes, approved by risk owner omar.haddad) expired on 2026-09-03, before the review time of 2026-10-12, so it cannot excuse the MFA deviation.
The CI run on head f280478 has result 'failure' (172 tests, 1 failure): the registered MFA-1 control test fails. No test exercises the new reopen path.
Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1, covering routes.py at e5bf646) lapses because this change alters routes.py behaviour. Its replacement, the exhaustive route control test, fails.

reopen_payee calls _audit, which records actor, action, target and time. However, the only registered AUD-1 evidence is a sample test that does not exercise reopen, which is below the exhaustive evidence required.
The new UPDATE in Store.reopen_payee is a fixed string literal with payee_id bound as a parameter, and the exhaustive test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed in the change's CI run.
Store.reopen_payee only updates status and closed_at and writes no NPI fields. The exhaustive test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed in the change's CI run.
Ticket CHG-25756 was approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-04, before the change opened. Its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover all four touched files.
The code_review approval comes from sofia.santos, a payments change_approver, who is a different person from the author mara.costa (who has no other alias among the approvers).
Both approvals name the head commit f280478, the change's only commit.
The change touches security-sensitive components (http, routes, store). A security_review approval from security_reviewer ines.halvorsen names the head commit.
The diff touches only application code (app.py, routes.py, service.py, store.py) and no controls data, control tests or CI paths, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency (emergency=false, ticket type 'standard'), so no post-implementation review is due.

summary: The change exposes a new privileged route, POST /payees/{id}/reopen (action manage_payees), without MFA, which violates MFA-1. The exception it relies on, EXC-0210, expired on 2026-09-03, before the review. The change's own CI run on the head commit fails the registered exhaustive MFA control test, so the testing requirement is not met, and the earlier MFA-1 evidence has lapsed with no valid replacement. The process records (ticket, independent code review, security review) are in order, but the violated obligations require rejection.
